units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
She is transfigured.

I have got rid of the bribe of bread. I have got rid of the bribe of heaven. Let God's work be done for its own sake: the work he had to create us to do because it cannot be done except by living men and women. When I die, let him be in my debt, not I in his; and let me forgive him as becomes a woman of my rank.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Then the way of life lies through the factory of death?
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Yes, through the raising of hell to heaven and of man to God, through the unveiling of an eternal light in the Valley of The Shadow.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Seizing him with both hands.

Oh, did you think my courage would never come back? did you believe that I was a deserter? that I, who have stood in the streets, and taken my people to my heart, and talked of the holiest and greatest things with them, could ever turn back and chatter foolishly to fashionable people about nothing in a drawingroom? Never, never, never, never: Major Barbara will die with the colors. Oh! and I have my dear little Dolly boy still; and he has found me my place and my work. Glory Hallelujah!
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She kisses him.
My dearest: consider my delicate health. I cannot stand as much happiness as you can.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Yes: it is not easy work being in love with me, is it? But it's good for you.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She runs to the shed, and calls, childlike.
Mamma! Mamma!
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Bilton comes out of the shed, followed by Undershaft.
I want Mamma.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: She is taking off her list slippers, dear.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: He passes on to Cusins.
Well? What does she say?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: She has gone right up into the skies.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: LADY BRITOMART [coming from the shed and stopping on the steps, obstructing Sarah, who follows with Lomax.
Barbara clutches like a baby at her mother's skirt].
Barbara: when will you learn to be independent and to act and think for yourself?
I know as well as possible what that cry of "Mamma, Mamma," means.
Always running to me!
SARAH [touching Lady Britomart's ribs with her finger tips and imitating a bicycle horn] Pip!
Pip!
LADY BRITOMART [highly indignant] How dare you say Pip! pip! to me, Sarah?
You are both very naughty children.
What do you want, Barbara?
I want a house in the village to live in with Dolly.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Dragging at the skirt.
Come and tell me which one to take.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [to Cusins] Six o'clock tomorrow morning, my young friend.
